Consonant inventories, chapter 1A, is moderately small
Vowel quality inventories, chapter 2A, is large vowel inventory (7-14)
Consonant-vowel ratio, chapter 3A, is low
Voicing in plosives and fricatives, chapter 4A, is voicing contrast in plosives alone
Voicing and gaps in plosive systems, chapter 5A, is /p t k b d g/
Uvular consonants, chapter 6A, is no uvulars
Glottalized consonants, chapter 7A, is no glottalized consonants
Lateral consonants, chapter 8A, is /l/, no obstruent laterals
Front rounded vowels, chapter 11A, is none
Syllable structure, chapter 12A, is moderately complex syllable structure
Tone, chapter 13A, is no tones
Fixed stress locations, chapter 14A, is no fixed stress (mostly weight-sensitive stress)
Weight-sensitive stress, chapter 15A, is not predictable
Weight factors in weight-sensitive stress systems, chapter 16A, is lexical: lexical stress, diacritic weight
Rhythm types, chapter 17A, is absent: no rhythmic stress
Absence of common consonants, chapter 18A, is all present
Presence of uncommon consonants, chapter 19A, is none
Order of subject and verb, chapter 82A, is subject precedes verb (sv)
Order of object and verb, chapter 83A, is object precedes verb (ov)
Order of adposition and noun phrase, chapter 85A, is more than one adposition type with none dominant
Order of genitive and noun, chapter 86A, is genitive-noun (genn)
Order of adjective and noun, chapter 87A, is modifying adjective follows noun (nadj)
Order of demonstrative and noun, chapter 88A, is demonstrative word follows noun (ndem)
Order of numeral and noun, chapter 89A, is numeral follows noun (nnum)
Relationship between the order of object and verb and the order of adposition and noun phrase, chapter 95A, is languages not falling into one of the preceding four types
Relationship between the order of object and verb and the order of adjective and noun, chapter 97A, is object-verb and noun-adjective (ov&nadj)
Negative morphemes, chapter 112A, is negative affix
Order of negative morpheme and verb, chapter 143A, is optional double negation
Optional double negation, chapter 143C, is (neg)[v-neg]
Preverbal negative morphemes, chapter 143E, is preverbal negative word
Postverbal negative morphemes, chapter 143F, is negative suffix
Minor morphological means of signaling negation, chapter 143G, is no negative tone infix or stem change
Position of negative word with respect to subject, object, and verb, chapter 144A, is optional double negation
The position of negative morphemes in sov languages, chapter 144L, is sov with optional double negation
Optional double negation in sov languages, chapter 144O, is sv & ov &  (neg)[v-neg]

Fixed stress locations, chapter 14A, is no fixed stress (mostly weight-sensitive stress)
Weight-sensitive stress, chapter 15A, is unbounded: stress can be anywhere in the word
Weight factors in weight-sensitive stress systems, chapter 16A, is long vowel: long vowels are heavy for stress

Consonant inventories, chapter 1A, is average
Vowel quality inventories, chapter 2A, is average vowel inventory (5-6)
Consonant-vowel ratio, chapter 3A, is average
Voicing in plosives and fricatives, chapter 4A, is voicing contrast in both plosives and fricatives
Voicing and gaps in plosive systems, chapter 5A, is /p t k b d g/
Uvular consonants, chapter 6A, is no uvulars
Glottalized consonants, chapter 7A, is no glottalized consonants
Lateral consonants, chapter 8A, is /l/, no obstruent laterals
The velar nasal, chapter 9A, is velar nasal, also initially
Vowel nasalization, chapter 10A, is contrastive nasal vowels absent
Front rounded vowels, chapter 11A, is none
Syllable structure, chapter 12A, is complex syllable structure
Tone, chapter 13A, is no tones
Fixed stress locations, chapter 14A, is penultimate: stress is on the penultimate (second from the right) syllable
Weight-sensitive stress, chapter 15A, is fixed stress (no weight-sensitivity)
Weight factors in weight-sensitive stress systems, chapter 16A, is no weight, or weight factor unknown
Rhythm types, chapter 17A, is trochaic: left-hand syllable in the foot is strong
Absence of common consonants, chapter 18A, is all present
Presence of uncommon consonants, chapter 19A, is none
Fusion of selected inflectional formatives, chapter 20A, is exclusively isolating
Exponence of selected inflectional formatives, chapter 21A, is no case
Exponence of tense-aspect-mood inflection, chapter 21B, is monoexponential tam
Inflectional synthesis of the verb, chapter 22A, is 4-5 categories per word
Locus of marking in the clause, chapter 23A, is p has no marking
Locus of marking in possessive noun phrases, chapter 24A, is possessor has no marking
Locus of marking: whole-language typology, chapter 25A, is consistently zero-marking
Zero marking of a and p arguments, chapter 25B, is zero-marking
Prefixing vs. suffixing in inflectional morphology, chapter 26A, is predominantly suffixing
Reduplication, chapter 27A, is full reduplication only
Case syncretism, chapter 28A, is inflectional case marking is absent or minimal
Syncretism in verbal person/number marking, chapter 29A, is no subject person/number marking
Number of genders, chapter 30A, is none
Sex-based and non-sex-based gender systems, chapter 31A, is no gender system
Systems of gender assignment, chapter 32A, is no gender system
Coding of nominal plurality, chapter 33A, is plural by complete reduplication of stem
Occurrence of nominal plurality, chapter 34A, is plural in all nouns, always optional
Plurality in independent personal pronouns, chapter 35A, is person-number stem
The associative plural, chapter 36A, is special non-bound associative plural marker
Definite articles, chapter 37A, is demonstrative word used as marker of definiteness
Indefinite articles, chapter 38A, is no indefinite article but definite article
Inclusive/exclusive distinction in independent pronouns, chapter 39A, is inclusive and exclusive differentiated
Inclusive/exclusive distinction in verbal inflection, chapter 40A, is no person marking at all
Distance contrasts in demonstratives, chapter 41A, is two-way contrast
Pronominal and adnominal demonstratives, chapter 42A, is same forms
Third person pronouns and demonstratives, chapter 43A, is third person pronouns and demonstratives are unrelated to demonstratives
Gender distinctions in independent personal pronouns, chapter 44A, is no gender distinctions
Politeness distinctions in pronouns, chapter 45A, is second person pronouns are dominantly avoided for politeness reasons
Indefinite pronouns, chapter 46A, is generic-noun-based indefinites
Intensifiers and reflexive pronouns, chapter 47A, is intensifiers and reflexive pronouns are formally identical
Person marking on adpositions, chapter 48A, is adpositions without person marking
Number of cases, chapter 49A, is no morphological case-marking
Asymmetrical case-marking, chapter 50A, is no morphological case-marking
Position of case affixes, chapter 51A, is neither case affixes nor adpositional clitics
Comitatives and instrumentals, chapter 52A, is mixed
Ordinal numerals, chapter 53A, is first/one-th: all ordinal numerals are derived from cardinal numerals with different allomorphs for 'first' one of which is morphologically independent of 'one'
Distributive numerals, chapter 54A, is no distributive numerals
Numeral classifiers, chapter 55A, is numeral classifiers are optional
Conjunctions and universal quantifiers, chapter 56A, is formally similar, involving interrogative expression
Position of pronominal possessive affixes, chapter 57A, is no possessive affixes
Obligatory possessive inflection, chapter 58A, is no obligatorily possessed nouns
Number of possessive nouns, chapter 58B, is none reported
Possessive classification, chapter 59A, is no possessive classification
Genitives, adjectives and relative clauses, chapter 60A, is weakly differentiated
Adjectives without nouns, chapter 61A, is adjective may occur without noun, obligatorily marked by preceding word
Action nominal constructions, chapter 62A, is ergative-possessive: s/p treated as possessors, a treated differently
Noun phrase conjunction, chapter 63A, is with-languages: 'and' and 'with' are identical
Nominal and verbal conjunction, chapter 64A, is nominal and verbal conjunction are largely identical
Perfective/imperfective aspect, chapter 65A, is no grammatical marking of perfective/imperfective distinction
The past tense, chapter 66A, is no grammatical marking of past/non-past distinction
The future tense, chapter 67A, is no inflectional marking of future/non-future distinction
The perfect, chapter 68A, is perfect derived from word meaning 'finish' or 'already'
Position of tense-aspect affixes, chapter 69A, is tense-aspect suffixes
The morphological imperative, chapter 70A, is the language has no morphologically dedicated second-person imperatives at all
The prohibitive, chapter 71A, is the prohbitive uses the verbal construction of the second singular imperative and a sentential negative strategy not found in (indicative) declaratives
Imperative-hortative systems, chapter 72A, is the language has neither a maximal nor a minimal system
The optative, chapter 73A, is inflectional optative absent
Situational possibility, chapter 74A, is the language can express situational possibility with affixes on verbs
Epistemic possibility, chapter 75A, is the language cannot express epistemic possibility with verbal constructions or with affixes on verbs, but with other kinds of markers
Overlap between situational and epistemic modal marking, chapter 76A, is the language has no markers that can code both situational and epistemic modality
Semantic distinctions of evidentiality, chapter 77A, is no grammatical evidentials
Coding of evidentiality, chapter 78A, is no grammatical evidentials
Suppletion according to tense and aspect, chapter 79A, is no suppletion in tense or aspect
Suppletion in imperatives and hortatives, chapter 79B, is none (= no suppletive imperatives reported in the reference material)
Verbal number and suppletion, chapter 80A, is no singular-(dual)-plural pairs/triples
Order of subject, object and verb, chapter 81A, is subject-verb-object (svo)
Order of subject and verb, chapter 82A, is subject precedes verb (sv)
Order of object and verb, chapter 83A, is object follows verb (vo)
Order of object, oblique, and verb, chapter 84A, is verb-object-oblique (vox)
Order of adposition and noun phrase, chapter 85A, is prepositions
Order of genitive and noun, chapter 86A, is noun-genitive (ngen)
Order of adjective and noun, chapter 87A, is modifying adjective follows noun (nadj)
Order of demonstrative and noun, chapter 88A, is demonstrative word follows noun (ndem)
Order of numeral and noun, chapter 89A, is numeral precedes noun (numn)
Order of relative clause and noun, chapter 90A, is relative clause follows noun (nrel)
Postnominal relative clauses, chapter 90C, is noun-relative clause (nrel) dominant
Order of degree word and adjective, chapter 91A, is degree word precedes adjective (degadj)
Position of polar question particles, chapter 92A, is question particle in either of two positions
Position of interrogative phrases in content questions, chapter 93A, is mixed, some interrogative phrases obligatorily initial, some not
Order of adverbial subordinator and clause, chapter 94A, is adverbial subordinators which are separate words and which appear at the beginning of the subordinate clause
Relationship between the order of object and verb and the order of adposition and noun phrase, chapter 95A, is verb-object and prepositional (vo&prep)
Relationship between the order of object and verb and the order of relative clause and noun, chapter 96A, is verb-object and noun-relative clause (vo&nrel)
Relationship between the order of object and verb and the order of adjective and noun, chapter 97A, is verb-object and noun-adjective (vo&nadj)
Alignment of case marking of full noun phrases, chapter 98A, is neutral
Alignment of case marking of pronouns, chapter 99A, is neutral
Alignment of verbal person marking, chapter 100A, is accusative alignment
Expression of pronominal subjects, chapter 101A, is pronominal subjects are expressed by pronouns in subject position that are normally if not obligatorily present
Verbal person marking, chapter 102A, is person marking of only the p argument
Third person zero of verbal person marking, chapter 103A, is no zero realization of third person s forms
Order of person markers on the verb, chapter 104A, is a and p do not or do not both occur on the verb
Ditransitive constructions: the verb 'give', chapter 105A, is mixed
Reciprocal constructions, chapter 106A, is all reciprocal constructions are formally distinct from reflexive constructions.
Passive constructions, chapter 107A, is there is a passive construction
Antipassive constructions, chapter 108A, is no antipassive
Productivity of the antipassive construction, chapter 108B, is no antipassive
Applicative constructions, chapter 109A, is benefactive object only; transitive base only
Other roles of applied objects, chapter 109B, is no other roles (= only benefactive)
Periphrastic causative constructions, chapter 110A, is sequential type but no purposive type
Nonperiphrastic causative constructions, chapter 111A, is morphological type but no compound type
Negative morphemes, chapter 112A, is negative word, unclear if verb or particle
Symmetric and asymmetric standard negation, chapter 113A, is symmetric standard negation only: type sym
Subtypes of asymmetric standard negation, chapter 114A, is non-assignable (no asymmetry found)
Negative indefinite pronouns and predicate negation, chapter 115A, is negative indefinites co-occur with predicate negation
Polar questions, chapter 116A, is question particle
Predicative possession, chapter 117A, is topic possessive
Predicative adjectives, chapter 118A, is predicative adjectives have verbal encoding
Nominal and locational predication, chapter 119A, is split (i.e. different) encoding of nominal and locational predication
Zero copula for predicate nominals, chapter 120A, is zero copula is possible
Relativization on subjects, chapter 122A, is gap
Relativization on obliques, chapter 123A, is gap strategy
'want' complement subjects, chapter 124A, is the complement subject is left implicit
Purpose clauses, chapter 125A, is balanced
'when' clauses, chapter 126A, is balanced
Reason clauses, chapter 127A, is balanced
Utterance complement clauses, chapter 128A, is balanced
Hand and arm, chapter 129A, is differentiation: one word denotes 'hand' and another, different word denotes 'arm'
Finger and hand, chapter 130A, is differentiation: one word denotes 'hand' and another, different word denotes 'finger' (or, very rarely, 'fingers')
Numeral bases, chapter 131A, is decimal
M-t pronouns, chapter 136A, is no m-t pronouns
M in first person singular, chapter 136B, is no m in first person singular
N-m pronouns, chapter 137A, is no n-m pronouns
M in second person singular, chapter 137B, is m in second person singular
Tea, chapter 138A, is words derived from min nan chinese te
Order of negative morpheme and verb, chapter 143A, is negv
Preverbal negative morphemes, chapter 143E, is preverbal negative word
Postverbal negative morphemes, chapter 143F, is no postverbal negative morpheme
Minor morphological means of signaling negation, chapter 143G, is no negative tone infix or stem change
Position of negative word with respect to subject, object, and verb, chapter 144A, is snegvo
Position of negative words relative to beginning and end of clause and with respect to adjacency to verb, chapter 144B, is immediately preverbal
The position of negative morphemes in svo languages, chapter 144D, is snegvo
Negsvo order, chapter 144H, is svo but negsvo does not occur
Snegvo order, chapter 144I, is separate word, no double negation
Svnego order, chapter 144J, is svo, but svnego does not occur
Svoneg order, chapter 144K, is svo but svoneg does not occur

The morphological imperative, chapter 70A, is the language has morphologically dedicated second singular as well as second plural imperatives
The prohibitive, chapter 71A, is the prohbitive uses the verbal construction of the second singular imperative and a sentential negative strategy not found in (indicative) declaratives
Imperative-hortative systems, chapter 72A, is the language has neither a maximal nor a minimal system
The optative, chapter 73A, is inflectional optative absent
Ditransitive constructions: the verb 'give', chapter 105A, is indirect-object construction

Numeral classifiers, chapter 55A, is numeral classifiers are absent
Adjectives without nouns, chapter 61A, is adjective may occur without noun, and without marking
The morphological imperative, chapter 70A, is the language has morphologically dedicated second singular as well as second plural imperatives
The prohibitive, chapter 71A, is the prohibitive uses a verbal construction other than the second singular imperative and a sentential negative strategy not found in (indicative) declaratives
